gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-arabi: Relaxed and rounded, Delius Unicase never thins or swells a stroke. Noto Sans Arabic sits underneath with wide openings and a pronounced x-height, so a long passage would move along cleanly and without any fuss.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-avest: Inviting and loose, Delius Unicase traces every letter with one constant line. Noto Sans Avestan feels cooler beside it, its curve tips left open and its lowercase tall, a clean modern counterweight to all that handwriting.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-balin: Rope-ladder spacing, handwritten charm. Noto Sans Balinese reads smoothly underneath, with breathing room inside each curve and short ascenders, so a stretch of text feels tidy and modern rather than crowded.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Relaxed from the first letter, Delius Unicase keeps every stroke at a single width. Noto Sans Bamum then carries a long passage cleanly, its big open counters and curves that stop before turning inward keeping the text light.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-bassa: Noto Sans Bassa Vah is businesslike and contemporary, with a dominant midsection and an open-jawed c. Delius Unicase, in contrast, keeps curves and straights the same line width, so a long stretch of the sans-serif body reads steadily.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-benga: Relaxed and handwritten, Delius Unicase gives its crossbars the same thickness as its stems, with rope-ladder spacing between letters. Noto Sans Bengali stays quieter, its capitals barely taller than lowercase.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-bhaik: Approachable from the first glance, Noto Sans Bhaiksuki has plump lowercase like tightly coiled rope and easily readable open apertures. gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-brahm: Flat, friendly handwriting with no tapering at all. Noto Sans Brahmi counters with a high mean line and open-ended curves, and its crisp contemporary tone against the single-weight heading is what makes the pair memorable.
